_source: Claude-authored DRAFT (2026-07-27), except the first rehireCard line, which is canonical from the design doc. NOT ported from reference/term-sheet-happens.jsx — that file was missing at authoring time.
rehireCard: Somehow, you've been hired again. The industry has no long-term memory.
A rival firm calls your track record 'contrarian experience.' You start Monday.
Your references were not checked. Welcome aboard.
zombieFundJabs: Your fund is described at a conference as 'technically still deploying.'
LPs receive your quarterly letter and file it under fiction.
A founder asks if your firm still does deals or just newsletters.
vetoLines: 'Love the energy. Hate the deal.' Your partner is already leaving.
Your partner slides the term sheet back unsigned, folded into a crane.
'We're pattern-matching here, and the pattern is no.'
founderWalkLines: The founder thanks you for your time in a tone that bills for it.
'We're actually oversubscribed.' The round closes without you by Friday.
The founder shakes your hand warmly and signs with your rival in the lobby.
vetoHeartbreak: The partnership passed on {company}. {company} did not return the favor to obscurity.
{company}, vetoed at the table, is now a unicorn with a waiting list of term sheets.
Somewhere a partner is explaining why passing on {company} was 'discipline.'
poachLines: A rival firm saw your DPI and mistook it for skill. Welcome to the partner track.
Poached. The recruiter used the word 'visionary' unprompted.
Your new firm announces your arrival with a blog post nobody asked for.
lpOfferQuirks: The anchor LP requires a monthly phone call with their nephew.
Capital calls are answered within ninety days, weather permitting.
The LP base is one university endowment and one unexplained yacht.
A side letter grants the family office veto power over your font choices.

wipeout: A bonfire with a management fee.
The capital was deployed. That much is certain.
underwater: Technically a fund, mathematically a donation.
The LPs have started calling it tuition.
respectable: Nobody got rich. Nobody got deposed. A wash, with expenses.
The rare fund that returns exactly what everyone quietly expected.
heater: The LPs return your calls before voicemail now.
Somewhere, a fund-of-funds slide features your logo.
legend: They will teach this fund at business schools that rejected you.
The endowment sends a fruit basket and a much larger check.

boardSeatLocked: Board seats are a Partner privilege. You may observe the parking lot.
Associates don't get board seats. Associates get the follow-up email.
finalCardPitches: It's basically your fund, but younger, and with AI.
We move fast, we break things, we've never heard of you.
The thesis is vibes-forward. The deck is nineteen slides of momentum.
enlightenmentLines: The LPs have stopped asking questions. The questions now come to you.
There is nothing left to prove, which is exactly when the industry starts listening.
Your quarterly letter is forwarded like scripture.
creditsLines: The fees continue whether you do or not.
Somewhere, a first-time founder is practicing your name.
The industry has no long-term memory. You, however, kept a ledger.

wipeout: I turned {fund} into {returned} at {firm}. The LPs call it tuition. Term Sheet Happens.
{dpi} DPI. The fund is a candle now. Term Sheet Happens.
I ran {firm} into the ground and all I kept was this PNG. Term Sheet Happens.
underwater: Returned {returned} of {fund} at {firm}. Technically a fund, mathematically a donation. Term Sheet Happens.
{dpi} DPI at {firm}. The LPs have stopped replying-all. Term Sheet Happens.
My fund did {dpi}. The industry has no long-term memory, so neither do I. Term Sheet Happens.
respectable: {dpi} DPI at {firm}. Nobody got rich, nobody got deposed. Term Sheet Happens.
Returned {returned} on {fund}. A wash, with expenses. Term Sheet Happens.
heater: {dpi} DPI at {firm}. The LPs answer before voicemail now. Term Sheet Happens.
Returned {returned} on {fund}. Currently accepting apologies. Term Sheet Happens.
legend: {dpi} DPI on {fund} at {firm}. They'll teach this one. Term Sheet Happens.
Returned {returned} to LPs in one fund. The endowment sent fruit. Term Sheet Happens.

lines: Your career went to trash. You retire to a soy farm very far from every major city. Maybe in a few years you'll return with a fake name and try once again.
The LPs' lawyers have lawyers. You change your name, move to Portugal and take up pottery.
Your Patagonia vest has been repossessed. Your LinkedIn now says "exploring what's next."
You returned less than nothing. Even the fees are suing you. You open a food truck under an assumed name.
Board seats, plural. Lawsuits, plural. You fake your own sabbatical and are never heard from again.
careerOver.cta: Start over with a fresh name
shareLines: My VC career ended in legal fees after {funds} funds. Term Sheet Happens.
I took too many board seats. The lawyers took the rest. Term Sheet Happens.

shareCareerLines: I've returned {returned} to LPs. Term Sheet Happens.
{returned} returned to LPs across {funds} funds. The fees were extra. Term Sheet Happens.
Career to date: {returned} back to LPs. You may now pitch me. Term Sheet Happens.
portfolioEmpty: No positions yet. Your LPs are paying 2% for vibes.
Nothing signed. Technically a perfect track record.

swordPull.title: Final offer
intros: Your number is below theirs. Only a true dealmaker can pull the term sheet from the stone.
The founder won't budge. Prove your conviction: pull the sword.
Legend says whoever pulls this sword gets pro rata rights.
won: The sword is yours. So are the terms.
The stone yields. So does the founder.
lost: The stone keeps the sword. The founder keeps the cap table.
Not worthy. The founder takes the bigger fund's call.
You pulled. The sword did not. Neither did the founder.

wheel.title: Final offer
intros: Spin the wheel of fortune. Stop it on yellow. The founder will be watching. You won't.
Remember where the yellow is. Then spin it blind. This is due diligence.
Land the pointer on yellow and the founder signs. Miss and they take the other term sheet.
won: Right on the yellow. Pure instinct. Definitely not luck.
Bullseye. You'll call it pattern matching in the podcast.
lost: Red. The founder takes the other term sheet.
So close. In venture, close is a polite word for zero.

vetoChallenge.title: Leadership challenge
intros: Your partner challenges your decision on a coin flip.
Your partner refuses to sign, but will accept the judgement of a quarter.
Your partner proposes the firm's most rigorous diligence process: a coin.
won: Called it. Your partner signs, visibly annoyed.
The coin agrees with you. Conviction confirmed, scientifically.
lost: Wrong call. The coin has spoken, and it sides with your partner.
The coin votes no. Your partner pockets it as a keepsake.
highLowIntros: Your partner deals one card face up. Call the next one: higher or lower.
Your partner's diligence process turns out to be a deck of cards. Higher or lower?
Your partner offers a compromise: one card, higher or lower, no further questions.
highLowWon: Right call. Your partner signs, muttering something about card counting.
The deck agrees with you. Your partner signs the term sheet face down.
highLowLost: Wrong call. Your partner reshuffles and leaves for lunch.
The deck sides with your partner. The term sheet goes back in the drawer.
diceIntros: Your partner produces a single die from a vest pocket. Even or odd?
Your partner proposes the firm's investment committee: one die, even or odd.
Your partner rolls for it. Call it: even or odd.
diceWon: Right call. Your partner signs and pockets the die for the next IC.
The die agrees with you. Your partner calls it 'data-driven'.
diceLost: Wrong call. Your partner blows on the die, satisfied.
The die votes no. Your partner logs it as 'process'.
sticksIntros: Your partner hides two sticks in a fist. The longer one decides the deal.
Your partner insists on drawing straws. Pick the longer stick.
Your partner's conviction is measured in sticks. Choose the long one.
sticksWon: Longest stick. Your partner signs, measuring twice to be sure.
You drew long. Your partner concedes and blames the ruler.
sticksLost: Short stick. Your partner keeps the long one as a pointer for the next meeting.
You drew short. The term sheet is shorter still.

fundIDifficulty.label: SOFT LANDING
fundIDifficulty.blurb: Small fund, long calendar, LPs who still believe in you. Practically a grant.

fundIDifficulty.label: BRUTAL
fundIDifficulty.blurb: Too much money, too few meetings, LPs already drafting the email.

lpRequests.title: LP requests
lpRequests.rewardNote: Meet them all to keep your seat at this firm. +{trust} LP trust each.

onThesis: Stay on thesis. They read the deck.
On-thesis only. It's in the LPA.
dryPowder: Keep {pct}% dry powder. Just in case.
unicorn: Bring home one unicorn. A real one.
returnFund: Return {x}x. The LPs did the math.
coolDeals: Skip the hype: heat {heat} or lower

lpRequests.verdictAllMet: All LP requests met: the firm wants you back.
lpRequests.verdictMissed: LP requests missed: start polishing the résumé.
lpRequests.noDealsNote: No investments, no credit: staying home doesn't count.
lpRequests.verdictForgiven: LP requests missed, but the returns did the talking: the firm will look the other way.
lpRequests.verdictFolded: Requests or not, at this DPI the firm is folding.

profile.title: Professional profile
profile.name: You
aboutByStage: Passionate about disruption. Mostly my own.
Investor. Board member. Has opinions about seed.
profile.empty: No experience yet. Every legend starts as a junior associate.

onboarding.about: Ready to start a journey in the VC world. Experience in disruptive, fast-growing businesses such as local organic refreshing-beverage pop-up stores.

bigChecks.label: BIG CHECKS
bigChecks.blurb: Bigger fund, same calendar. More money to deploy, more to explain.

dealFlow.label: DEAL FLOW
dealFlow.blurb: More founders than you can count, a smaller fund to count them with.

lpDarling.label: LP DARLING
lpDarling.blurb: Same fund, but the LPs adore you. Spend it before they read the memo.

megaFund.label: MEGA FUND
megaFund.blurb: Colossal fund, junior title. Nobody here knows your name yet.

rehire.intro: Stay at your firm and keep climbing, or leave for a new firm and new opportunities.
rehire.sealedRange: Funds between {lo} and {hi}, LP trust between {tlo} and {thi}.
rehire.sealedLp: {n} LP packages are waiting: funds between {lo} and {hi}. Your own firm, at last.
rehire.sealedNote: You won't know which one you got until you open the envelope.
rehire.stayLocked: Unmet LP requests. The LPs have asked for a word.
rehire.stayForgiven: LP requests missed, but nobody argues with these returns.
rehire.stayFolded: {firm} has shut down. The LPs pulled the plug; the plants are already for sale.
